title: Why No Two Living Things Match

scenes.visual: Ten oak leaves in a row, a ruler line shows different lengths; two questions with question marks.
scenes.tts: Pick ten leaves from one white oak. Every leaf has rounded lobes. But measure them with a ruler, and you will almost surely find different lengths and shapes. So why is no living thing exactly like another? And are all mutations bad?
scenes.narration: Pick ten leaves from one white oak. Every leaf has rounded lobes. But measure them with a ruler, and you will almost surely find different lengths and shapes. So why is no living thing exactly like another? And are all mutations bad?

scenes.visual: Leaves in a population outline; same basic shape, small length differences marked; word variation.
scenes.tts: A trait is a feature of a living thing, such as color, shape or height. A population is a group of the same kind of living thing in one area. Members of a population share the same basic features. But they differ in many traits. Variation means the differences among members of a population.

scenes.visual: Two stacked bars: same blue gene blocks, different teal food and health blocks, different total heights (in this sketch).
scenes.tts: Some variation comes from genes. Many genes carry the code for a protein. Some variation comes from the environment. Height shows both. Many genes add a little to height. Food and health during childhood matter too. So two children with very similar genes can grow to different heights.

scenes.visual: A row of base blocks, one turns orange, protein shape changes; three cause chips; chance chip, crossed out needs chip.
scenes.tts: New genetic variation starts with a mutation. A mutation is a change in the D N A sequence, the order of the bases. It can change the protein a gene codes for. Copying mistakes, radiation, or some chemicals can cause mutations. Mutations are random. Random means they happen by chance, not because a living thing needs them.

scenes.visual: Parent outline with body cells and sex cells; a mutation in a skin cell stays; one in a sex cell travels to the child box.
scenes.tts: Where a mutation happens matters. Body cells are all the cells of the body except eggs, sperm and the cells that make them, such as skin cells. Sex cells are eggs and sperm. A mutation in a skin cell stays in that person. A mutation in a sex cell can pass to offspring, the young.

scenes.visual: A recipe card with one changed line; three outcomes help, harm, no difference; answer.
scenes.tts: Does a mutation help? That often depends on the living thing and where it lives. Think of a misprint in a recipe. Most misprints change little. Some ruin the dish. A rare one makes it better. But a recipe has a writer, and no one chooses a mutation. A mutation can help, harm or make no difference. So not all mutations are bad.
